correctness.rationale: For all m>=3 and integer 5N/8<b<=N, polar-form symplectic reduction shows every nonzero quadratic support of size <3N/8 is a codimension-two affine flat. Projection on the two high bits, fiber hyperplane bounds, and the strict 3Q/2 interval threshold identify exactly eight possible supporting arcs of length Q. Their unique zero gap has length 3Q; precisely max{3Q-b+1,0} zero windows determine the stated full coefficient distribution. The sharp endpoint construction gives a new nonconsecutive flat. Replayed independent exact word/window enumeration in dimensions 3..5 and affine-flat census in 3..8 corroborate the complete proof. No general conclusion is based only on enumeration.

value.rationale: Complete b-symbol coefficient distribution for a natural infinite family and a continuum of high read widths in a classical error-correcting code; exactly eight exceptional minimum-weight codewords independent of dimension, sharp five-eighths transition and a structural explanation via ordered affine flats. These multiplicities are not implied by the previously known RM minimum-distance formula; they quantify the near-saturation of the b-symbol channel across the code and are natural coding-theoretic invariants, not arbitrary isolated parameters.
